title: Modernizing Spectrum Sharing for Satellite Broadband
description:
In this document, the Space Bureau (Bureau or we) within the Federal Communications Commission (Commission) updates the initial set of geostationary (GSO) satellite network reference links adopted in the Modernizing Spectrum Sharing for Satellite Broadband Report and Order (Order). Ensuring the GSO reference links appropriately reflect typical and widespread GSO satellite operations in the United States will promote efficient spectrum sharing among today's broadband satellite systems.

 

Effective 7 December 2026.

title: Significant New Use Rules on Certain Chemical Substances (25- 3.5e)
description:
The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is issuing significant new use rules (SNURs) under the Toxic Substances Control Act (TSCA) for certain chemical substances that were the subject of premanufacture notices (PMNs) and are also subject to an Order issued by EPA pursuant to TSCA. The SNURs require persons to notify EPA at least 90 days before commencing the manufacture (defined by statute to include import) or processing of any of these chemical substances for an activity that is designated as a significant new use in the SNUR. The required notification initiates EPA's evaluation of the conditions of that use for that chemical substance. In addition, the manufacture or processing for the significant new use may not commence until EPA has conducted a review of the required notification; made an appropriate determination regarding that notification; and taken such actions as required by that determination.

 

This rule is effective on 4 January 2027. For purposes of judicial review, this rule shall be promulgated at 1 p.m. Eastern Standard Time (EST) on 19 November 2026.

 

91 Federal Register (FR) 69704, 5 November 2026; Title 40 Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) Part 721:
https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2026-11-05/html/2026-22576.htm
https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2026-11-05/pdf/2026-22576.pdf

 

This final rule and previous actions notified under the symbol G/TBT/N/USA/2289 are identified by Docket Number EPA-HQ-OPPT-2025-2169. The Docket Folder is available from Regulations.gov at https://www.regulations.gov/docket/EPA-HQ-OPPT-2025-2169/document and provides access to primary and supporting documents as well as comments received. Documents are also accessible from Regulations.gov by searching the Docket Number.

title: Notice of intent: Change to the veterinary omeprazole listing on the Prescription Drug List.
description: The purpose of this Notice of Intent is to announce that Health Canada will add a qualifier to the "Omeprazole or its salts" listing on the veterinary use part of the Prescription Drug List on April 30, 2027. The intent is to allow for the non-prescription use of omeprazole when sold to prevent gastric ulcers in horses at a dosage of less than 2 mg/kg/day. Health Canada received a veterinary drug submission for an omeprazole product indicated to prevent gastric ulcers in horses at a dosage below 2 mg/kg/day. After reviewing the safety and efficacy information included in the submission, it was determined that omeprazole, when used for the noted purpose and at this dosage, does not meet the criteria for prescription status outlined in section C.01.040.3 of the Food and Drug Regulations. This amendment will be in effect on 30 April 2027 and will be communicated through the posting of a Notice of Amendment on the Health Canada website.

title: Regulations Amending the Clean Fuel Regulations (43 pages, available in English and French)
description:
The Clean Fuel Regulations (the Regulations) require regulated parties (producers and importers of gasoline or diesel) to reduce the lifecycle carbon intensity of the gasoline or diesel they produce or import for use in Canada. To achieve this, the Regulations establish annual lifecycle carbon intensity limits for gasoline and diesel in grams of carbon dioxide equivalent emitted per unit of energy (expressed as grams per megajoule or gCO2e/MJ). The annual lifecycle carbon intensity limits came into force on July 1, 2023 and gradually decreases until 2030.  

 

The Regulations establish a credit market as the primary compliance mechanism. Each credit represents a lifecycle emission reduction of one tonne of CO2e. For each compliance period, a regulated party must create or acquire sufficient credits and use them to demonstrate compliance with its annual reduction requirements. Credits are created for the following categories of actions: 

  • Category 1: Emission reduction projects along the fuel lifecycle (e.g. carbon capture and permanent storage, low-carbon intensity electricity, co-processing at refineries)
  • Category 2: Supply of low-carbon fuels for use in Canada (e.g. ethanol, biodiesel, hydrogenation derived renewable diesel, renewable natural gas or renewable propane)
  • Category 3: Supplying fuel and energy in advanced vehicle technologies (e.g. electricity and hydrogen) 

 

The proposed Regulations Amending the Clean Fuel Regulations (the proposed Amendments) would introduce a credit multiplier for liquid low-carbon fuel produced in Canada that is derived from a feedstock that was harvested, produced, extracted, or collected and processed in North America. A multiplier is also being proposed for gaseous low carbon fuel produced in Canada that is used as a fuel or energy source in a vehicle. 

These multipliers provide additional credit value for Canadian produced low carbon fuel made with North American feedstocks and range from 1.3 to 1.8. In practical terms, this means eligible Canadian produced fuels would create more compliance credits, helping Canadian producers compete on a more level playing field with fuels supported by foreign incentives and encouraging investment in domestic production.

 

In addition, the proposed Amendments would reserve half of the 10% limit on the use of gaseous compliance credits for the Canadian production of gaseous low-carbon fuel such as renewable natural gas. This helps ensure that a portion of the Canadian market remains available for Canadian produced gaseous low carbon fuel, supporting domestic production and investment.

 

The proposed Amendments also aim to provide increased compliance flexibility to regulated parties and support the long-term stability and resilience of the credit market. To achieve this, the proposed Amendments would increase the limit for the use of compliance credits created from contributions to registered emission-reduction funding programs from 10% to 15%. This gives regulated parties more options to meet their compliance obligations and can help lower compliance costs while continuing to achieve emission reductions. Other minor administrative modifications are also proposed.

objectivesFreeText:
The objective of the proposed Amendments is to support the Canadian low-carbon fuel sector while maintaining the Regulations’ primary objective of reducing GHG emissions and supporting Canada’s transition to a lower-carbon economy. A strong and healthy domestic low-carbon fuel sector is an important contributor to Canada's long-term decarbonization objectives and provides a key compliance pathway for the Regulations, supporting GHG emission reductions now and into the future. 

 

The proposed Amendments also aim to provide increased compliance flexibility to regulated parties and support the long-term stability and resilience of the credit market. Lastly, the proposed Amendments aim to improve credit market efficiency, support more transparent pricing of credits, and reduce regulatory burden.

title: Norma Oficial Mexicana de Emergencia NOM-EM-023-SE-2026, Industria del cemento-Cementos hidráulicos-Especificaciones de calidad, métodos de prueba e información comercial.
description: The notified Emergency Mexican Official Standard establishes the specifications, test methods, commercial information and conformity assessment procedure for hydraulic cements used in the construction sector that are manufactured in, imported into and/or marketed in national territory, in order to ensure the safety of users of these products.Scope of application:The Emergency Mexican Official Standard applies to hydraulic cements that are manufactured in, imported into and/or marketed in national territory.The Standard includes the classification of cements according to their composition, compressive strength and special characteristics; physical and chemical specifications; sampling and test methods; certification schemes; commercial information requirements; and monitoring and verification provisions.
productsFreeText:
Cementos hidráulicos utilizados en el sector de la construcción que se fabriquen, importen y/o comercialicen en territorio nacional.

La NOM-EM-023-SE-2026 es de observancia obligatoria y comprende los siguientes tipos de cemento, clasificados de acuerdo con su composición:

  • Cemento Portland Ordinario (CPO).
  • Cemento Portland Puzolánico (CPP).
  • Cemento Portland con Escoria Granulada de Alto Horno (CPEG).
  • Cemento Portland Compuesto (CPC).

Lo anterior, en sus distintas clases de resistencia a la compresión y, cuando corresponda, con características especiales de resistencia a los sulfatos, baja reactividad álcali agregado, bajo calor de hidratación y blancura, conforme a lo establecido en la norma.

title: Short Range Devices – Specifications (Third Revision) (MCMC MTSFB TC T007:2026)
description:
This Technical Code was developed for the purpose of certifying communications equipment under the Communications and Multimedia (Technical Standards) Regulations 2000 [P.U.(A) 124/2000]. 

This Technical Code specifies the technical requirements for SRDs operating in the frequency bands defined in the relevant Standard Radio System Plans and the latest Class Assignments issued by the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC). The SRDs may be fixed, mobile or portable stations fitted with an antenna connector or an integral antenna.

This revision updates the frequency bands, maximum RF output power, and transmitter and receiver spurious emission limits for new generation SRDs, taking into account industry requirements and the latest MCMC Class Assignments. It also removes marking, interoperability, Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC) and electrical safety requirements from this Technical Code, as those baseline requirements are now addressed separately in MCMC MTSFB TC T022, Communications Equipment - Baseline Requirements.
productsFreeText:
Short Range Devices (SRDs) which may be fixed, mobile or portable stations that are fitted with an antenna connector or an integral antenna. 

 

The applications include various generic short-range devices not limited to, inductive applications, active medical implant devices, alarm system, inductive devices, Industrial Scientific and Medical (ISM), Radio Frequency Identification (RFID), security devices, Ultra-Wideband (UWB) communication devices, UWB automotive radar devices, UWB radar imaging devices, wireless microphones and wireless power.

 

Radiocommunications (ICS:33.060)
objectivesFreeText:
The objective of this Technical Code is to establish clear and up-to-date technical requirements for the certification of SRDs under the Communications and Multimedia (Technical Standards) Regulations 2000, and to ensure that SRDs placed on the Malaysian market operate within permitted frequency bands and power limits.

The revision is intended to align the SRD technical requirements with the latest MCMC’s Class Assignments and relevant Standard Radio System Plans, accommodate new generation SRD technologies and industry requirements, promote efficient spectrum use, and minimise the risk of harmful interference to radiocommunications services while supporting safety and regulatory certainty for equipment certification.

There are no urgent problems applicable to this notification.

title: Communications Equipment – Baseline Requirements (MCMC MTSFB TC T022:2026)
description:
This Technical Code was developed for the purpose of certifying communications equipment under the Communications and Multimedia (Technical Standards) Regulations 2000 [P.U.(A) 124/2000]. 

This Technical Code establishes the minimum baseline requirements for all communications equipment, including but not limited to user equipment, network facilities and radiocommunications equipment, for use in communications services in Malaysia. It is to be read together with other applicable technical codes on communications equipment and serves as the baseline requirement for communications equipment that is not covered by any specific technical code.

This Technical Code covers operational requirements, including the requirement that equipment shall not cause interference to authorised radiocommunication services and shall tolerate interference from other radiocommunication services, electrical or electronic equipment. It also specifies general requirements on marking, interoperability and keypad layout, and technical requirements relating to Radio Frequency (RF), Internet Protocol version 6 (IPv6), Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC), electrical safety, Specific Absorption Rate (SAR) and Power Density (PD). 

This Technical Code also differentiates between directly connected and non-directly connected Short Range Devices (SRDs), with directly connected SRDs required to comply with applicable IPv6, safety, EMC and SAR requirements.
productsFreeText:
All communications equipment, including (but not limited to) user equipment, network facilities, and radiocommunications equipment.

(Telecommunications. Audio and Video Engineering) (ICS:33)
objectivesFreeText:
The objective of the Technical Code is to provide a harmonised baseline framework for the certification and compliance of communications equipment under the Communications and Multimedia (Technical Standards) Regulations 2000. It is intended to streamline the compliance process and enhance the quality, interoperability and electrical safety of communications equipment used in Malaysia.

The rationale for establishing these baseline requirements is to address the continued growth of the communications market and rapid technological advancement in communications equipment, while ensuring that such equipment operates safely, does not cause harmful interference to authorised radiocommunication services, can function satisfactorily in its electromagnetic environment, supports relevant network and IP-based requirements, and complies with applicable human exposure and electrical safety limits. 

No urgent problems are applicable.

title: Pipeline Safety: Amendments to Liquefied Natural Gas Facilities
description: Notice of proposed rulemaking - The Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration (PHMSA) proposes updating its regulations for liquefied natural gas (LNG) facilities to incorporate by reference the most recent industry safety standards and to make other changes to account for more than two decades of improvements and technological advancements. title: Draft Amendment of the Chemicals Act
description:
The national poison center provides important services to the public and healthcare professionals in cases of poisoning. However, the center’s funding is not adequately regulated. The current Chemicals Act provides for the designation and financial support of a poison center by the federal government. 
It should be amended so that chemical manufacturers are required to operate and finance a central poison center. A similar obligation should also be imposed on authorization holders for medicinal products and enshrined in the Therapeutic Products Act. The government should continue to provide financial support to the poison center.

description:
[Annex 2] Several radio interface regulations (RIR) are amended in line with the latest developments and European harmonization.

Following radio interface regulations are amended (784.101.21/ …):

  • RIR0501-33: Private IMT networks in the frequency range 3400 – 3500 MHz (Non-Public Network (NPN)) adjusted due to the new terms of use.
  • RIR0510-01: Safety-Related Intelligent Transport Systems (ITS) in the frequency range 5875 - 5925 MHz aligned with ECC/DEC/(08)01.
  • RIR1007-01: Model control in the frequency range 26990 - 27200 kHz aligned with ERC/REC 70-03, Annex 8.
  • RIR1007-02: Model control in the frequency range 34.995 - 35.225 MHz aligned with ERC/REC 70-03, Annex 8.
  • RIR1007-03: Model control in the frequency range 40.660 - 40.700 MHz aligned with ERC/REC 70-03, Annex 8.
  • RIR1009-02: Radio microphones in the frequency range 174 - 223 MHz aligned with ERC/REC 70-03, Annex 10.
  • RIR1009-10: Radio microphones in the frequency range 470 - 694 MHz aligned with ERC/REC 70-03, Annex 10.
  • RIR1101-25: Amateur in the frequency range 70.0 - 70.5 MHz adjusted due to the termination of the sole PMR licence of 70.0375 – 70.1125 MHz, which lies between two existing amateur bands: A: 70.0000 - 70.0375 MHz and B: 70.1125 - 70.5000 MHz.

New radio interface regulations (784.101.21/ …):

  • RIR1108-07: Bird radar in the frequency range 9370 - 9430 MHz

title: Draft Commission Delegated Regulation amending Regulation (EC) No 1272/2008 of the European Parliament and of the Council as regards the addition of notes
description:
The purpose of this draft proposal for a Commission Delegated Regulation under Article 53(1) of the CLP Regulation is to amend Part 1, section 1.1.3, of Annex VI to introduce notes clarifying the application of certain harmonised classifications introduced pursuant to Article 37(7) of the CLP Regulation, in particular as regards the classification of mixtures containing substances covered by the same Annex VI entry for ED, PBT and vPvB hazard classes and differentiations, including through additivity rules applicable to specific groups of substances. 

 

This notification should be read in conjunction with the complementary notification concerning the harmonised classification and labelling of certain substances (26 pages including Annex, in English), which establishes the underlying harmonised classifications for approximately 107 substances identified as ED, PBT or vPvB under REACH, the Plant Protection Products Regulation and the Biocidal Products Regulation, to which the notes introduced by this act apply.

title: Government Regulation No. 40 of 2026 amending Government Regulation No. 42 of 2024 on the Implementation of Halal Product Assurance
description:
Government Regulation No. 40 of 2026 amending Government Regulation No. 42 of 2024 on the Implementation of Halal Product Assurance revises Articles 160 and 161 concerning the phased implementation of mandatory halal certification.

  • Article 160 extends the phase-in period for food, beverages, slaughter products and slaughtering services provided by micro and small enterprises until 17 October 2028. Mandatory halal certification for these products and services originating from abroad begins on 18 October 2028, taking into consideration the completion of mutual recognition arrangements for halal certificates. For medium and large enterprises, certification of related services, excluding slaughtering services, also begins on 18 October 2028. Paragraph (4) is deleted.
  • Article 161 extends the phase-in period until 17 October 2028 for natural medicines, quasi-drugs, health supplements, cosmetics, chemical and genetically engineered products, specified consumer goods and Class A medical devices. The deadlines remain 17 October 2029 for over-the-counter and limited over-the-counter medicines and Class B medical devices, and 17 October 2034 for prescription medicines excluding psychotropics, and Class C medical devices. Related services follow the schedules of the respective products, and businesses may apply for certification before the applicable phase-in period ends.

Pursuant to Article II, the provisions governing the assurance of conformity of foreign halal products entering the territory of Indonesia are repealed and declared no longer in force. Consequently, Regulation of the Halal Product Assurance Organizing Agency (BPJPH) No. 4 of 2026 on the Assurance of Conformity of Foreign Halal Products Entering the Territory of Indonesia, previously notified under G/TBT/N/IDN/190 and G/TBT/N/IDN/190/Add.1, is repealed and no longer in force.
productsFreeText: Food and beverages; traditional medicines and health supplements; medicinal products; cosmetics; chemical products; genetically engineered products; clothing, headgear and accessories; household appliances; moslems worship equipment; stationery and office equipment; goods for medical devices risk class A, B, and C.
objectivesFreeText: To ensure information of products in the market is sufficient in assuring halal integrity for Muslim consumer. As the country with largest Muslims population in the world, the Government is responsible to provide a reliable system for the citizens concerned with their needs for Halal Products Assurance

title: Unleashing the Power of Unlicensed Ultra-Wideband Devices; Petition of Robert Bosch LLC for Amendment of the Part 15 Subpart F Ultra-Wideband Rules; and Petition of Alliance for Automative Innovation et al. To Amend Part 15 of the FCC's Rules To Permit the Operation of Certain Ultra-Wideband Devices
description: Proposed rule - The Federal Communications Commission (Commission or FCC) proposes to update its rules for Ultra-Wideband (UWB) devices to reflect significant technological developments since the rules were first adopted in 2002. UWB technology has matured into a widely used, low-power enabler that supports applications in tracking, automation, precision location, health monitoring, athletic performance, and public safety. As capabilities of UWB have expanded, the existing rules have not kept pace with the technological change, resulting in an increasing number of waiver requests received by the Commission to authorize modern devices. The Notice of Proposed Rulemaking seeks comment on revisions intended to modernize the UWB framework, provide greater flexibility for future applications, promote continued innovation, and ensure the protection of incumbent federal and non-federal spectrum users.

title: Infant Formula Nutrient Requirements
description: Proposed rule - The Food and Drug Administration (FDA or we) proposes to amend the regulations on nutrient specifications and labeling for infant formula as part of its phased, comprehensive review of infant formula nutrients. This action, if finalized, would amend the minimum and/or maximum levels of four required nutrients, change the unit of measure for certain nutrients, change the permitted source to meet one of the nutrient requirements, and amend the content of the required labeling. This action also includes a comprehensive assessment of four additional nutrients for which we conclude that the current required levels remain appropriate and reflect the best available scientific evidence on infant nutritional requirements and safe intake levels.

title: Significant New Use Rules on Certain Chemical Substances (26-7)
description: Proposed rule - The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is proposing significant new use rules (SNURs) under the Toxic Substances Control Act (TSCA) for certain chemical substances that were the subject of premanufacture notices (PMNs) and are also subject to an Order issued by EPA pursuant to TSCA. Once finalized, the SNURs would require persons who intend to manufacture (defined by statute to include import) or process any of these chemical substances for an activity that is proposed as a significant new use by this rulemaking to notify EPA at least 90 days before commencing that activity. The required notification initiates EPA's evaluation of the conditions of that use for that chemical substance. In addition, the manufacture or processing for the significant new use may not commence until EPA has conducted a review of the required notification, made an appropriate determination regarding that notification, and taken such actions as required by that determination.

title: Proposal to modify the Table of Chemical, Physical and the Nutritional Characteristics of Food
description:
Health Canada’s Food and Nutrition Directorate has launched a consultation regarding the notice of proposal to modify the Table of Chemical, Physical and Nutritional Characteristics of Food (Table).

The Food and Drug Regulations (FDR) include requirements related to protein quality that apply to the conditions for making protein content statements and claims and to the composition of foods in certain categories. The Table sets out the values (for example, protein ratings) and corresponding method(s) of analysis for demonstrating compliance with the these requirements. The “Digestible Indispensable Amino Acid Score” (DIAAS) method is not currently permitted to demonstrate compliance with these protein quality requirements. The “Protein Digestibility Corrected Amino Acid Score” (PDCAAS) method is permitted, however the prescribed methodology does not permit the use of protein digestibility values derived from in vitro assays (that is, non-human/animal). 

As described in the notice, Health Canada is proposing to authorize the use of the DIAAS method and two in vitro assays to determine protein digestibility values when using the PDCAAS method.

The modifications to the Table would come into force the day they are published on Health Canada’s website and would include:

  • the listing of the DIAAS method in the Table;
  • the incorporation by reference into the FDR (through the Table) of the document Determination of the protein rating using the Digestible Indispensable Amino Acid Score (DIAAS); and 

the modifications to the incorporated by reference document Determination of the protein rating using the Protein Digestibility Corrected Amino Acid Score (PDCAAS).

objectivesFreeText: The purpose of this communication is to publicly announce the Department's intention in this regard and to provide the appropriate contact information for those wishing to submit comments, inquiries or new scientific information relevant to this proposal.

title: Draft Commission Delegated Regulation amending Regulation (EC) No 1272/2008 of the European Parliament and of the Council as regards the harmonised classification and labelling of certain substances
description:
The purpose of this draft proposal for a Commission Delegated Regulation under Article 37(7) of Regulation (EC) No 1272/2008 on classification, labelling and packaging of substances and mixtures (the CLP Regulation) is to amend Table 3 of Part 3 of Annex VI to the CLP Regulation by introducing entries for substances already assessed under other Union legislation, in particular those identified as endocrine disruptors (ED), persistent, bioaccumulative and toxic (PBT), or very persistent and very bioaccumulative (vPvB) under Regulation (EC) No 1907/2006 (REACH), Regulation (EC) No 1107/2009 (Plant Protection Products Regulation) and Regulation (EU) No 528/2012 (Biocidal Products Regulation), thereby avoiding duplication of hazard assessments and ensuring that approximately 107 substances are included in Annex VI of the CLP Regulation. 

 

This notification should be read in conjunction with the complementary notification concerning the addition of notes to Part 1, section 1.1.3, of Annex VI (6 pages including Annex, in English), which introduces notes clarifying how the harmonised classifications established by this act are to be applied in practice, in particular as regards the classification of mixtures and the use of additivity rules for specific groups of substances.

objectivesFreeText: Protection of human health and the environment, ensuring the proper functioning of the EU internal market; and avoiding duplication of the assessment of hazardous properties of substances by relying on existing evaluations carried out under other Union legislation.

title: Decision on withdrawal of approval of the active substance Dimethomorph in GB
description:
The decision to withdraw approval of the active substance dimethomorph in Great Britain was adopted on 16 October 2026, published on 30 October 2026, and will enter into force on 30 November 2026. In accordance with Art. 21 (1) of Assimilation Regulation 1107/2009, the following grace periods will apply:

 • Existing authorisations for sale and supply of plant protection products containing dimethomorph will be withdrawn on 31 May 2027. 

• The grace period for storage, disposal and use of those products will expire on 31 May 2028.
productsFreeText:
Dimethomorph (pesticide active substance); 

Pesticides and other agrochemicals (ICS code(s): 65.100)

objectives.name: Protection of human health or safety (TBT)
Protection of animal or plant life or health (TBT)

objectivesFreeText:
Active substances must be approved before they can be used in plant protection products.  Assimilated Regulation No 1107/2009 (concerning the placing of plant protection products on the market, “the Regulation”) lays down criteria for approval in Article 4 and Annex II.  These criteria must be satisfied in order to protect human and animal health, and the environment.

The competent authority undertook a review of the GB approval of dimethomorph under Article 21(1) of the Regulation.  The review considered endocrine disrupting properties for the oestrogen, androgen and steroidogenesis (EAS) modalities in humans and classification as toxic for reproduction category 1B for effects on fertility (Points 3.6.5 and 3.6.4 of Annex II of the Regulation respectively).

The competent authority concluded that dimethomorph failed to meet the approval criteria provided for in Article 4 of the Regulation and, in accordance with Article 21(5)(b), decided to withdraw the approval. 

Existing authorisations for sale and supply of plant protection products containing dimethomorph will be withdrawn six months after withdrawal of the active substance approval.  In accordance with Article 46 of Regulation 1107/2009, a grace period for storage, disposal and use of those products will expire twelve months later.

description:
The proposed amendments to the Regulation on the Permission, Notification, Review, Etc. of In Vitro Diagnostic Medical Devices are as follows:

A. Exemption from raw material declaration requirements in manufacturing (import) notifications for in vitro diagnostic equipment

B. Relaxation of requirements for clinical performance study data for IVD approval

C. Elimination of notarization requirements for translations of documents in foreign languages other than English

D. Expansion of the scope of exemption from sales business notification for in vitro diagnostic medical devices in response to public health crisis

E. Expedited review for re-applications of IVD approval

title: The  Turkish Food  Codex  Communiqué on the Distilled Alcoholic Beverages
description:
The  Turkish Food  Codex  Communiqué on  Distilled Alcoholic Beverages  was notified to the WTO through G/TBT/N/TUR/71/Rev.1 on 31 July 2025. 

The Communiqué  has been published in the Official Gazette dated 1 October 2026, numbered 33387. 

Provisional Article

(1) Food business operators operating before the publication date of this Communiqué shall comply with the provisions of this Communiqué by 1 July 2027.

(2) Food business operators operating before the publication date of this Communiqué shall comply with the provisions of the Communiqué repealed by Article 22 until they achieve compliance with the provisions of this Communiqué.

(3) Products placed on the market before the publication date of this Communiqué or for which official import controls have been completed before that date may remain on the market for eighteen months from the publication date of this Communiqué.

title: Turkish Food Codex Regulation on Food Additives
description:
Turkish Food Codex Regulation on Food Additives was notified to WTO through G/TBT/N/TUR/200 on 23/06/2022.

The purpose of this Regulation is to modify the content of previously notified Regulation. The main amendments introduced in this draft are:

 

Following the entry into force of the Turkish Food Codex Regulation on Food Additives (Official Gazette Date: October 13, 2023, Official Gazette No. 32338, Supplement), which is harmonised with Regulation (EC) No 1333/2008, Türkiye has continued to align its legislation with subsequent EU amendments. Türkiye has also introduced a number of additional amendments considered necessary under national conditions.

 

•   The conditions for the use of E 476 polyglycerol polyricinoleate have been revised, permitting its use in “03. Edible ices and ice cream” and in emulsified sauces falling under food category 12.6.

•   E 267, buffered vinegar, has been added to the regulations as a new food additive. This food additive, which serves as a preservative and acidity regulator, has been included in Group I, and its use is permitted at the “quantum satis” level.

•   For E 249–250 nitrites and E 251–252 nitrates, the maximum permitted levels for addition in various categories, including meat, processed fish products, and dairy products, have been reduced. Furthermore, to more effectively monitor the total dietary intake of nitrites and nitrates, maximum limits have been established for residue levels from all sources throughout the shelf life of final products ready for market; the unit of expression has been changed from chemical formulas (sodium nitrite or sodium nitrate) to NO₂ and NO₃ ions.

•   E 483 Stearyl tartrate has been removed from the list of approved food additives. With this regulation, authorizations for its use as an emulsifier in all previously permitted categories, including flavored fermented dairy products, baked goods, and confectionery, have been revoked.

•    E 345(i) Trimagnesium dicitrate has been incorporated into the regulations as a new food additive for use in the “17.1 Solid dietary supplements” category. E 345(i) functions as a stabilizer and anti-caking agent in solid dietary supplements.

•  The name of category 14.2.8 has been changed to “Other alcoholic beverages, including other distilled alcohol-based beverages with an alcohol content by volume of less than 15%.” In addition, changes have been made to the permitted uses of certain food additives (such as specific groups of colorants and stabilizers) in some traditional fermented alcoholic beverages produced in the EU.

•   E 334 Tartaric acid (L(+)-), E 335 Sodium tartrates, E 336 Potassium tartrates, E 337 Sodium potassium tartrate, and E 354 Calcium tartrate have been removed from Group I and are now permitted only in specific categories with specified maximum usage levels. Their use in food enzymes and flavourings has also been restricted in Annex III.

•  In the “16. Desserts” food category, the scope of use for E 200–202 Sorbic acid — potassium sorbate has been expanded to include water-based gelatine-based desserts.

•   The scope of use for E 460 Cellulose powder and E 575 Glucono-delta-lactone has been expanded to permit their use in unripened soft spreadable cheese products within the “01.7.6 Cheese products” food category.

•   In the “04.1.1 Whole fresh fruits and vegetables” food category, the authorization for surface applications of E 471 mono- and diglycerides of fatty acids and E 903 carnauba wax for glazing purposes has been extended to include passion fruit, kiwi, and cassava. E 322 Lecithins and E 570 Fatty acids have been authorized under Annex III as carriers in preparations intended for polishing cassava.

•   E 960b Steviol glycosides produced by fermentation have been added to the regulations as a new food additive. This amendment includes E 960b in the existing “E 960a–960d: Steviol glycosides” group, allowing this sweetener to be used under the same conditions as other steviol glycosides.

•  In Annex III, Section 5, Part B, the authorization for the use of E 466 sodium carboxymethyl cellulose (cellulose gum) has been revoked.

•  In Annex III, Section 5, Part B, the use of E 301 sodium ascorbate has been authorized in microencapsulated vitamin A preparations used in infant and follow-on formulas.

•   In Annex III, Section 1, the scope of use for E 1202 polyvinylpyrrolidone has been expanded to permit its use as a carrier in colouring tablets intended for the decorative colouring of eggshells.

•   In the food category “16. Desserts; excluding products falling under categories 1, 3, and 4,” the use of E 200–202 sorbic acid—potassium sorbate is permitted only in unheated plant-based mousses.

•   The use of E 999 Quillaia extract is permitted in both solid and liquid food supplements (Categories 17.1 and 17.2). Additionally, provisions have been added to Annex III to allow its use as an emulsifier in flavourings.

•   E 412 guar gum has been banned in the “13.1.1 Infant formula” food category.

•  The following additions have been made to the list of food categories under Section D of Annex II:

         •    18.1 Processed foods not covered by Categories 18.2 and 18.3, excluding foods for infants     

         and young children

         •   18.2 Meal-replacement foods intended for weight loss

         •   18.3 Foods specifically manufactured to reduce the gluten content of gluten-containing 

         ingredients or to substitute gluten-containing ingredients

•    The following food categories listed under Annex II, SECTION D have been deleted. Authority over these categories lies with the Ministry of Health.

        •    13.1.4 Special medical-purpose dietary foods for infants and young children, as defined in     

        the Turkish Food Codex Regulation on Special Medical-Purpose Dietary Foods / Special   

        formulas for infants

        •   13.1.4.1 Dietary foods for special medical purposes for newborns and special formulas for 

        newborns

        •    3.1.4.2 Dietary foods for special medical purposes for infants and young children as defined 

        in the Turkish Food Codex Regulation on Dietary Foods for Special Medical Purposes

        •   13.2 Dietary foods for special medical purposes as defined in the Turkish Food Codex 

        Regulation on Dietary Foods for Special Medical Purposes (excluding those listed in category 

        (13.1.4))

•   E 942 The sale of nitrous oxide to the end consumer is prohibited.

•  The phrase “Non-alcoholic wine-like products” has been removed from the name of the food category “14.2.2 Turkish Food Codex – Wine Regulation: Wine and Other Products.”

•   In the subcategories under the “08. Meat” category, the definition has been used instead of the word “sausage.” The term “sausage” (sausages) is used in EU countries to refer to meat products served in casings and is not limited to the narrower meaning used in Türkiye.

•    To prevent the uncontrolled use of sorbic acid and benzoates, which may be present due to carry over from ingredients in meatless çiğ köfte products, under the category “12.7 Salads and savoury/spiced spreads for sandwiches,” the following limits have been established for meatless çiğ köfte: E 200–202 Sorbic acid — potassium sorbate; E 210-113 Benzoic acid—benzoates at a maximum usage level of 200 mg/kg for each additive group. 

•    In the “14.1.1 Turkish Food Codex Regulation on Fruit Juices and Similar Products,” pickle brine has been excluded from the list of foods in the “Fruit Juices and Vegetable Juices” category where Group I food additives may be used. The use of E 210–213 (benzoic acid—benzoates) is permitted at a maximum level of 200 mg/l.

•    Additional restrictions have been introduced in Annex VI, titled “Certain Products Produced in Türkiye and Food Additives Prohibited in These Products.”

        •    In sucuk: water-holding agents in the E 400–469 range, E 235 natamycin, and E 553b 

         talc are prohibited.

        •    In heat-treated sucuk, the following are prohibited: E 400–469, E 235 natamycin, E 243 

        ethyl laurol arginate, and E 553b talc.

        •    In pastırma, raw or cooked döner, poultry döner, and raw or cooked meatballs and poultry 

        meatballs, E 400–469 are prohibited.

        •    All additives are prohibited in ground meat kavurma.

•   In Annex VI, titled “Certain Products Produced in Our Country and Food Additives Prohibited in These Products,” certain food additives are exempt from these restrictions.

        •    While the use of all food additives is prohibited in çiğ köfte, meatless çiğ köfte, and mezze 

        (such as haydari, Arnavut liver, fava beans, shakshuka, hummus, and similar dishes), E 267 

        (buffered vinegar) is exempt from this prohibition.

        •    While the use of all food additives is prohibited in köme, pestil, bastık, walnut-stuffed 

        sucuk, and similar products, as well as in baklava, E 330 citric acid is exempt from this 

        prohibition.

 

This Regulation enters into force on the date of its publication with a transitional period as December 31, 2028. Products placed on the market before 31/12/2028 by food businesses operating before the publication date of the Regulation establishing this article, and foods containing these products, may remain on the market until the end of their shelf life.

title: Safety Standard for Automatic Residential Garage Door Operators
description:
Direct final rule - In October 2025, updates to the entrapment protection provisions in the UL 325 standard were accepted under the Consumer Product Safety Improvement Act of 1990 (Improvement Act) for inclusion in the Commission's mandatory safety regulation for automatic residential garage door operators. In this direct final rule, the Consumer Product Safety Commission (Commission) is amending the Commission's automatic residential garage door operators mandatory regulation to align with the changes in UL 325. 
 

The rule is effective on 29 December 2026, unless the Commission receives significant adverse comments by 30 November 2026. If CPSC receives a timely significant adverse comment, the Commission will publish a notification in the Federal Register, withdrawing this direct final rule before its effective date. The incorporation by reference of certain material listed in this rule is approved by the Director of the Federal Register as of 29 December 2026. The incorporation by reference of certain other material listed in this rule was approved by the Director as of 9 May 2016.

 

91 Federal Register (FR) 68456, 30 October 2026, Title 16 Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) Part 1211:
https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2026-10-30/html/2026-22213.htm
https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/FR-2026-10-30/pdf/2026-22213.pdf

 

This direct final rule is identified by Docket Number CPSC-2015-0025.  The Docket Folder is available from Regulations.gov at https://www.regulations.gov/docket/CPSC-2015-0025/document and provides access to primary and supporting documents as well as comments received. Documents are also accessible from Regulations.gov by searching the Docket Number. WTO Members and their stakeholders are asked to submit comments to the USA TBT Enquiry Point by or before 4pm Eastern Time on 30 November 2026. Comments received by the USA TBT Enquiry Point from WTO Members and their stakeholders will be shared with CPSC and will also be submitted to the Docket on Regulations.gov if received within the comment period.

 

Previous actions notified under the symbol G/TBT/N/USA/1029 are also identified by Docket Number CPSC-2012-0054.

title: National technical regulation on automobile tachograph and automobiles driver image digital video recorder
description:
SUMMARY: 

 

The draft National Technical Regulation on automobile tachographs and driver image digital video recorders was previously notified to the WTO under document G/TBT/N/VNM/327 on 2 October 2024.

 

The notified measure has been substantially revised and its scope expanded to include passenger compartment image recording devices and integrated monitoring and recording devices installed on road vehicles. The revised draft comprises 59 pages in Vietnamese and is intended to replace QCVN 06:2024/BCA.

 

-Technical requirements: operational functions, status indication, hardware, recording and storage of journey data (at least 30 days) and image data (at least 3 days for driver images, at least 10 days for passenger compartment images), data transmission, information security, power supply and installation.

- Automatic detection: new requirements for artificial intelligence-based detection of unsafe behaviours and traffic violations by drivers and passengers, driver facial recognition, and audible (Vietnamese voice) warnings. Detection rate and accuracy must each be at least 90% for each behaviour.

- Data and security: requirements on journey data, images and video transmission, secure configuration and update of AI models, data extraction through wired or wireless interfaces, hardware protection and cybersecurity.

- Conformity assessment: conformity declaration based on conformity certification. Certification follows Method 7 for imported products and Method 5 for domestically produced products under Circular No. 14/2026/TT-BKHCN. 

- Transitional provisions: devices already installed on vehicles before entry into force may    continue to be used until 31 December 2029. Phased application: 1 January 2028 (driver image    devices for certain vehicle categories), 1 January 2029 (passenger compartment devices for vehicles over 29 seats), 1 January 2030 (passenger compartment devices for vehicles of 8 to    29 seats)..
